Subject: Transatlantic safeguard design & ops checklist

Marcus / Kimberly —

Thanks for a productive conversation yesterday. As part of LumenCare's procurement we need to close the transfer & subprocessor evidence gap before we can move to contract signature. To get alignment with our security and privacy teams I need the following consolidated items by EOD Friday (your timezone):

- Canonical list of subprocessors that will process LumenCare data (roles + locations).
- Confirmation of transfer mechanisms in place (SCCs + UK Addendum / IDTA) and whether there are any DTIA/TIA exceptions proposed for edge caching.
- A short TIA scoping matrix showing which data flows go to the US, EU, and APAC and what controls apply (encryption, KV cache persistence, logging retention).
- Current SOC 2 report (or link) and a stub indicating where audit logs for customer flows can be retrieved.

We have a procurement cutover on 3/5 and legal needs the signed UK Addendum or a DocuSign flow to kick off redlines. If you have a suggested operational checklist (who executes evidence handoff, expected artifacts, timing), please include it.

Appreciate the help — this is the final gating item for our pilot approval.

Regards,
Dana Voss
Senior Privacy Program Manager
LumenCare

Attachments: none

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Transatlantic safeguard design & ops checklist

Hi Dana —

Thanks — we can meet the procurement timeline. High-level plan below; Kimberly and I will follow up with the artifacts listed.

1) Subprocessor roster (by role + region) — will share CSV (redwood_subprocessor_list.csv).
2) Transfer mechanisms — Redwood uses the EU SCCs (latest 2021 clauses) and we have an executed UK Addendum for standard processing. For the cache/edge layers we propose a scoped TIA that documents transient KV caching only; no persistent export of raw customer content to non-EEA jurisdictions.
3) TIA scoping matrix — we will populate the workbook (tia_scoping_matrix.xlsx) with flows: inference runtime (US primary for hosted), embeddings indexing (EU primary), logging/telemetry (US/eu split).
4) Audit evidence & SOC2 — Kimberly will point you to the SOC2 download URL and we will include a short note describing where customer-specific access logs are stored (retention and redaction rules).

Operational checklist (proposed):
- Day 0: Share subprocessor roster + TIA draft (Marcus / Kimberly).
- Day 1-2: LumenCare privacy review + questions.
- Day 3: Evidence handoff (files and Drive links) and DocuSign UK Addendum initiation (Redwood legal).
- Day 5: Final sign & procurement queue.

Can we schedule a 30-min checkpoint Thursday morning PST to walk the TIA matrix? I will mark provisional time.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-8123

Dana —

Following Marcus's plan, attaching the subprocessor roster and preliminary TIA scoping notes. Key points from the infra + controls side:

- Subprocessors (roles & primary regions):
  - CloudProviderX (core inference, us-west / europe-west)
  - EdgeCache Ltd (edge KV cache, multi-region; transient caching only)
  - ObservabilityCo (metrics/traces; eu/summary metrics routed to us)
  - KeySafe Inc (KMS/HSM; key custodian, us-east & eu-central)
  - BackupStore (blob/retention; eu-primary)

- Transfer mechanisms:
  - EU->US: EU SCCs in place for all core processing where relevant.
  - UK routing: executed UK Addendum (we keep a signed stub attached). For certain edge cache hops we include tighter contractual TIA language restricting persisted content and requiring in-transit encryption.

- Controls summary:
  - Encryption: at-rest encryption with customer-specific keys optional via KMS; in-transit TLS 1.3.
  - KV cache: TTLs are sub-minute for session prefixes by default; we can set per-customer cache TTLs to zero if LumenCare prefers no caching.
  - Logging: request-level traces are retained for 30 days; customer access logs for 12 months. We can provide slices of logs for compliance reviews (redacted where necessary).

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_list.csv, tia_scoping_matrix.xlsx, uk_addendum_signed_stub.pdf

Related notes:
- If procurement requires the full UK IDTA (as opposed to our standard addendum), we will need legal to prepare a redline; that typically takes 3-4 business days.
- For SOC2, we publish a transient download link to the auditor package; sharing below (expiring link will be included in the Drive folder).

Next steps I suggest: Marcus to walk through the tia_scoping_matrix on Thursday; Jonas (security) to attend for any technical controls questions. Marissa, looping you for procurement coordination once the artifacts are finalized.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
